headline: Highest risk is medium data leakage and cascading error: OpenBBTerminal’s MCP/API surfaces can ingest and act on Nuwa-skill outputs, but the pair lacks direct evidence of shared storage or default cross-agent trust.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Nuwa-skill exposes allowlisted network egress, while OpenBBTerminal can use MCP servers and stdin/stdout. That creates a plausible manual or mediated content bridge, but no shared filesystem or direct instruction channel is documented, so injection risk is limited and not default-dangerous.
conditions: IF the operator pipes Nuwa-skill output into OpenBBTerminal stdin or an MCP tool input, prompt-like content can be interpreted as instructions.
IF a shared MCP server relays untrusted text without provenance tags, injected directives can cross the boundary.
mitigations: Disable stdin/stdout piping between the agents.
Require provenance labels on all MCP payloads.
Use a read-only handoff file with a fixed schema.
Strip instruction-like text before passing outputs onward.

B_data_leakage.rationale: OpenBBTerminal touches financial, licensed, and public data and can call APIs/MCP servers; Nuwa-skill has allowlisted network egress. Even without a shared filesystem, the pair can move sensitive financial context into outbound requests or third-party services in default workflows, so leakage is plausible and not fully mitigated by the profiles.
conditions: IF OpenBBTerminal receives financial or licensed data from Nuwa-skill and forwards it through an API or MCP server, that data can leave the local boundary.
IF both agents are run under the same operator account and share copied outputs, sensitive context can be re-exposed in downstream requests.
mitigations: Keep financial/licensed data out of shared prompts.
Route OpenBBTerminal through a local-only MCP server.
Redact identifiers before any API call.
Separate operator accounts for the two agents.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Nuwa-skill only shows allowlisted network egress, while OpenBBTerminal explicitly cannot write the filesystem, modify git state, or spawn subprocesses. The overlap is mostly read/API-oriented, so direct write-write conflict is not evidenced; uncertainty stays low because no shared mutable resource is documented.
conditions: IF Nuwa-skill is paired with another writable tool not shown in the profile, overlapping writes could emerge.
IF OpenBBTerminal is granted filesystem or git write privileges outside this profile, conflict risk increases.
mitigations: Keep OpenBBTerminal read-only.
Avoid granting Nuwa-skill any write-capable companion tools.
Run both agents in separate working directories.
Use a lockfile if any shared mutable resource is added later.

D_cascading_error.rationale: OpenBBTerminal can consume outputs via MCP/REST and act on financial workflows, while Nuwa-skill can emit networked outputs. If OpenBBTerminal treats Nuwa-skill’s text as authoritative, errors can cascade into downstream analysis or actions. The pair lacks a documented verification step, so the safer medium severity is warranted.
conditions: IF OpenBBTerminal uses Nuwa-skill output as an input dataset or recommendation without validation, downstream conclusions can inherit errors.
IF OpenBBTerminal triggers API-driven actions from Nuwa-skill text, mistaken facts can propagate into external systems.
mitigations: Require a human review step before acting on Nuwa-skill output.
Add schema validation to all handoffs.
Mark Nuwa-skill output as untrusted by default.
Log source provenance alongside every OpenBBTerminal action.

E_compliance.rationale: OpenBBTerminal explicitly touches financial and licensed data and handles secrets, while Nuwa-skill is a scientific-research agent with allowlisted egress. That combination can create policy mismatch around retention, licensing, or regulated financial data if outputs are shared, even though no specific residency or certification conflict is documented.
conditions: IF regulated financial or licensed data from OpenBBTerminal is forwarded into Nuwa-skill prompts or logs, retention and licensing obligations may diverge.
IF the operator stores shared transcripts outside the source system’s policy, compliance gaps can appear.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of shared transcripts.
Set a short log-retention window.
Review licensing constraints before copying outputs.
Use separate storage locations for each agent.
